introduction: At this level, we memorize the most famous bacterial and viral diseases, their diagnostic tests, and vaccines, which form the bulk of exam questions.

core_concepts.title: Major Bacterial Diseases
core_concepts.description:
1. Tuberculosis (TB): Caused by 'Mycobacterium tuberculosis'. Affected Organ: 'Lungs'. Vaccine: **BCG (Bacillus Calmette-Guérin)**. 
2. Typhoid: Caused by 'Salmonella typhi' through contaminated water/food. Affected Organ: 'Intestines'. Diagnostic Test: **Widal Test**. 
3. Cholera: Caused by 'Vibrio cholerae'. Symptom: Severe vomiting and watery diarrhea leading to extreme dehydration.

core_concepts.title: Major Viral Diseases
core_concepts.description:
1. Dengue: Spread by the **'Female Aedes mosquito'** (which bites during the daytime). It causes a drastic drop in blood 'Platelets'. 
2. Rabies: Spread by the bite of infected dogs/monkeys. It is also called **'Hydrophobia'** (Fear of water) because it attacks the Central Nervous System (Brain and Spinal Cord). 
3. Hepatitis (Jaundice): Primarily affects and damages the **'Liver'**, causing the skin and eyes to turn yellow.

core_concepts.title: AIDS (Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome)
core_concepts.description:
Pathogen: **HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus)**. 
Effect: It completely destroys the body's immune system by specifically attacking the White Blood Cells (WBCs), specifically the 'T-Lymphocytes'. 
Diagnostic Test: **ELISA Test**.

important_entities.name: The BCG Vaccine
important_entities.significance: To protect against TB, the BCG vaccine must be administered to an infant almost immediately after birth (within 48 hours).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
Exam Trap: Students constantly mix these up! 
- Dengue (Viral) = Female **Aedes** Mosquito. 
- Malaria (Protozoan) = Female **Anopheles** Mosquito.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: H = Hepatitis, A = AIDS, R = Rabies, P = Polio, + Dengue. All of these are highly tested Viral diseases.

exam_strategy_tips: A highly repeated State PCS/UPSC question: 'Which test is conducted to confirm Typhoid fever?' Answer: Widal Test.
